sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page east2696 + reference records 552847 (Wang 2011), 699566 (Wang 2020), 309627 (Lama 2012), 550905 (Moseley 2010); ISO 639-3 code page yit (change request 2007-076, name change only)
sources.note: Bibliographic/classificatory only; confirms Wang 2011 (225 pp, CNKI) and Wang 2020 (284 pp, Yunnan Renmin Chubanshe) as the only descriptive works; east2696 sits under 'Unclassified Core Lalu' at Xinping coordinates.

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2010. Lalo regional varieties: phylogeny, dialectometry, and sociolinguistics. PhD thesis, La Trobe University. doi:10.26181/21844209.v1
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonological sketches of 15 Lalo varieties (Central/Western/Eastern Core Lalo in Dali Prefecture; peripheral Mangdi, Eka, Yangliu, Xuzhang). No section on word stress anywhere; tone and phonation only. Sole incidental remark, p.64 (CW-QY, a Central Lalo variety = xish1235, not yit): 'Following a stressed syllable, the syllabic nasal loses its syllabicity and merges with the previous syllable'. Crucially the thesis has NO datapoint from Xinping/Jianxing (zero mentions of Xinping), so it does not describe the variety Glottolog files as east2696.

sources.citation: Lam, Edwin & Angel Lam. 2008. A working paper on the phonology of Lalu. SIL East Asia Group, unpublished ms.

sources.note: Only other 'Lalu' phonology sketch known; but per Yang 2010 it covers Eastern Lalo of Dali Municipality (Diaocao), a different Core Lalo variety -- useful only if Ethnologue's yit is taken to include Dali E Lalo.

Abstract: '韵母松紧对立..有三种调类；音节结构简单,全部为开音节；语流音变和句尾合音现象普遍' = tense/lax vowel contrast, three tone categories, all open syllables, pervasive sandhi/fusion. Full text (where any stress remark would sit, e.g. under 语流音变) not accessible.
